abstract.para: &kexec; starts a new kernel directly from the running kernel, without going through the firmware and the boot loader. A reboot with &kexec; is therefore faster than a normal reboot.

topic.para: The kexec command from the kexec-tools package loads the new kernel into memory through the kexec system call. The running kernel then hands control to it, so the firmware (BIOS/UEFI) initialization and the boot loader do not run.

listitem.para: Faster reboots. Skipping the firmware and the boot loader saves time, which matters if you reboot a system often, for example after kernel updates.
Booting another kernel once. You can load any kernel image with the kernel options you choose, without changing the boot loader configuration.

section.title: &kexec; and &kdump;
section.para: &kdump; also uses &kexec;, but in a different way. It loads a capture kernel with kexec -p, and that kernel starts only when the running kernel crashes. Normal reboots are not affected. &kdump; is described in the separate article Capturing and Analyzing Kernel Crash Dumps with Kdump.
